## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 39*, titled *Antovassa* ("Wandering during the rainy season"), is an ecclesiastical disciplinary rule belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule stipulates that a Buddhist nun (*bhikkhunī*) who travels on a journey or goes wandering during the rainy season commits an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the rule and its accompanying analysis has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Full parallels to the rule are preserved in several Buddhist Vinaya traditions. Within the Pali canon, the regulation corresponds directly to Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Pācittiya 39 and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pācittiya 39. Parallels in other lineages include the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 95* and its Pātimokkha), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 92* and its Pātimokkha), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 95* and its Pātimokkha), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 101* and its Pātimokkha), and Mahāsāṃghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc 134* and its Pātimokkha) in Chinese translation, as well as Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda versions (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc172* and its Pātimokkha) and a Sanskrit Lokottaravāda version (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc134*).
